newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Ausdoc buys NZ Freightways courier unit.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Ausdoc buys NZ Freightways courier unit.

text.p: Australian business services company Ausdoc Group Ltd said on Thursday it has agreed to buy the courier business of New Zealand's Freightways Ltd for NZ$125 million (US$80 million).
Ausdoc said Freightways' Express Freight Services group, the largest courier and express freight business in New Zealand, closely matched its own operations in Australia.
The purchase was conditional on the arrangement of funding, and approval by New Zealand regulatory bodies.
Ausdoc gave few details of how it would fund the acquisition, but said it was proposed that the equity proportion would be fully underwritten.
SBC Warburg and BT Securities have been engaged as lead managers it said.
Ausdoc requested trading in its shares be suspended shortly after the acquisition announcement, pending a further announcement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
The company said the New Zealand acquistion was expected to be earnings per share positive in the first 12 months of ownership after amortisation of A$3 million in goodwill.
"Accordingly, the directors of Ausdoc believe that the acquisition will be strongly cash earnings per share positive from the outset," it said in a statement.
Express Freight Services had gross revenues of about NZ$160 million in the year ended March 31, 1997, and earnings before interest and tax of about NZ$17.1 million.
Freightways is being broken up by its owner Tappenden Holdings, which tried to float the business three years ago, according to New Zealand press reports.
Its other major units, New Zealand's largest security firm Armourguard and a 66 percent stake in pallet hire business Chep New Zealand were sold last month.
